# Erdős #99 — Wave94 ROOT proof, source and provenance audit (2026-10-29)

**Scope and verdict.** For each `n`, an ORIGINAL set of `n` unit-separated
planar points globally minimizes its ORIGINAL diameter `D_n`. Does **EVERY**
sufficiently large such set have an EXACT ORIGINAL triple with all three
pairwise distances equal to 1? This is still **OPEN**; no all-global proof or
certified infinite globally optimal triangle-free counterfamily was obtained.
Official statement/status: https://www.erdosproblems.com/99 .

## Stronger finite hull theorem and asymptotic width, original global only

Native GPT-6 Sol Web High Herschel `01a188c3-2556-76f1-a14e-47cbd3a204d1`
supplied an improved width cap constant and candidate finite vertex bound;
independent native **Locke** `01a188ce-7c9e-7c43-b9fd-f26687146528`
COMPLETED/CLOSED, checked the previously doubtful quadratic branch and gave a
stronger *branch-free* finite estimate. ROOT checked their algebra, source
formulas and 500 high-precision sample inequalities in
`work/erdos99/audit-wave94-root.py` (PASS; analytic inequality established
below, samples are only a regression test).

Let `K=conv(P)`, `A=area(K)`, `L=perimeter(K)`, `D=D_n`, `m` the number of
ORIGINAL extreme vertices, and `w` the minimum width. Averaging translations
of a unit triangular lattice inside the *open* disk of diameter `D` proves
`n >= pi D^2/(2sqrt(3))+1`: otherwise some translate contains `n` unit-spaced
sites with strictly smaller diameter than the globally minimal `D`. Oler gives
`n <= 2A/sqrt(3)+L/2+1`; therefore

```
pi D^2/4 - A <= (sqrt(3)/4)L.
```

Reinhardt's perimeter bound for an `m`-gon of diameter `D` is
`L <= 2m D sin(pi/(2m))`, and polygon isoperimetry gives
`A <= L^2/[4m tan(pi/m)]`. Hence

```
A <= (m/2) cos(pi/m) tan(pi/(2m)) D^2.
```

Let `x=pi/(2m)`, `0<x<=pi/6`, and
`delta_m=pi/4-(m/2) cos(2x) tan(x)
        =pi/(4x)*(x-sin(2x)+tan(x))`.
Alternating Taylor for `sin(2x)` and the positive Taylor coefficients of
`tan(x)` give
`delta_m >= (5pi/12)x^2*(1-2x^2/25)`.
Also `sin x <= x*(1-2x^2/25)` for `x<=pi/6`: use
`sin x<=x-x^3/6+x^5/120` and `x^2<=pi^2/36<10.4`.
Combining the area deficit inequality and the Reinhardt perimeter estimate,
cancel the strictly positive factor `1-2x^2/25`, obtaining the **finite**
original-global theorem

```
m^2 >= [5pi^2/(12sqrt(3))] D
    = 2.374257815735023488... D.       (n>=3)
```

The previously proposed bound with subtraction `2pi^2/25` also holds but is
weaker. This finite statement strengthens the earlier *asymptotic* Wave73
bound, with the **same** leading coefficient `m>=1.540862... sqrt(D)`;
do not claim a novel asymptotic constant or a proof of Erdős #99.

For width, `K-K` lies in `B(0,D) intersect {|y|<=w}`. Brunn–Minkowski gives
`4A<=area(K-K)`, hence exact circular two-cap deficit

```
arccos(w/D) - (w/D)sqrt(1-(w/D)^2) <= sqrt(3)pi/(2D).
```

With `epsilon=(D-w)/D`, the left side is
`(4sqrt(2)/3)epsilon^(3/2)*(1+O(epsilon))`. Consequently

```
w >= D-[(3pi sqrt(6)/16)^(2/3)+o(1)]D^(1/3)
  = D-[1.276883220553783026...+o(1)]D^(1/3).
```

This improves earlier Wave90 constant `1.60877...` as a bound from the cap
inequality. No bound on exact contact graph triangles follows from either.
Source attributions: Oler (1961) https://doi.org/10.4153/CMB-1961-018-7 ;
Reinhardt (1922), reproduced Mulansky–Potschka (2026)
https://doi.org/10.1007/s10107-025-02244-x . The combination and constants
above are internal deductions of Herschel/Locke/ROOT, *not attributed to the
published authors as their own theorem*. Historical priority unchecked.

## Nine original points — stronger global lower, independently feasible upper

WebAgentGPT `w93_894` job `38ab6dd4-46e7-40fe-967c-535a45fca368`
proposed a two-hull-order Oler/Reinhardt bound; independent native Pasteur
`01a188c3-6d9d-7883-8806-bf9908265a8a` checked `D9>=2.30389534755...`
and proposed a **Wegner improvement**. Independent native GPT-6 Sol Web High
**Hooke** `01a188d1-aa64-7e53-af3c-f32e20aa6c78` COMPLETED/CLOSED and
separately checked every published inequality and equality condition.

For any ORIGINAL 9-point unit-separated set of diameter `D`, if the hull has
`m>=8` extremes, each hull edge has length >=1 and the Reinhardt perimeter
bound yields
`D>=1/(2sin(pi/16))=2.562915447741506...`.
For `m<=7`, pad vertices by collinear subdivisions or limits. Reinhardt's
regular odd-heptagon upper bounds give

```
A <= a7 D^2, a7=7 sin^2(pi/14) cot(pi/7)=0.719740926545929...
L <= b7 D,   b7=14 sin(pi/14)=3.115293075388402...
```

For 9 disks of radius 1/2 centered at these original points, the authors'
restatement of **Wegner's inequality** (with essential integer ceiling
`ceil(sqrt(12n-3)-3)=8` at `n=9`), and Steiner's formula for the Minkowski
offset of the centers' hull, yield `A+L/2 >= 4+2sqrt(3)`.
Thus `a7 D^2+(b7/2)D>=4+2sqrt(3)`, whose positive root is

```
D_* = 2.315183288447548262441117023676... .
```

**Strictness:** Equality would require the original hull to be a regular
heptagon to saturate both Reinhardt estimates, whereas equality in Wegner is
a Wegner/Groemer packing and has a hull with at most six sides. This
contradiction excludes equality, and compactness of the global minimization
gives `D9 > D_*` (not merely each feasible D>D_* with unattained infimum).
The FULL ORIGINAL unrestricted global minimum is not determined.

ROOT opened and visually checked p.3 of the primary Böröczky–Ruzsa (2007)
manuscript, Theorem 1.1, with the ceiling and equality case, and p.2 with
the six-sided Groemer equality classification:
https://www.renyi.hu/~carlos/wegner.pdf . Original Wegner (1986)
https://real-j.mtak.hu/5463/1/StudScientMath_21.pdf ; Reinhardt reproduced
by Mulansky–Potschka https://doi.org/10.1007/s10107-025-02244-x .
The n9 bound is a **derived consequence**, not credited as published in
either paper; novelty/priority unestablished.

Two separately audited *feasible*, not globally proved optimal, ORIGINAL
9-point configurations:

1. Pasteur parameter witness `(t=455922/10^7, h=12846185/10^7)`:
   `work/erdos99/audit-wave93-n9.py` proves all **11** unit edges by exact
   algebraic identities and bounds all **25** other distances strictly above
   1 with rational root enclosures; the unique diametral pair is P6-P7 of
   exact length `2h=2.569237`. The previous version of this script used only
   interval straddling for unit pairs: ROOT corrected that certification gap.
2. Hooke exact integer-over-square-root certificate: nine ORIGINAL points
   `(0,0),(1091184431,0),(2091184431,0),
   (545592216,+/-838050795),(1440342065,+/-1284618490),
   (2384780327,+/-955929626)`, each coordinate divided by `sqrt(q)` with
   `q=999999998503135826`. ROOT independently enumerated all 36 integer
   squared separations: minimum `q` (twice only), maximum
   `6600978659399520400` (P6-P7), hence diameter exactly
   `sqrt(6600978659399520400/q)=2.569236981922899397...<2.569237`.
   The two unit edges preclude any exact unit equilateral triple.

ROOT `work/erdos99/audit-wave94-root.py` PASS independent rational distances,
all displayed high-precision numerical values, and inequality regression.
The previous Wave91 internal `D9<2.569236981` record is *numerically stronger*
than Hooke's newly independent exact rational witness: do **not** represent
Hooke's example as improving that prior ceiling. Neither finite example
certifies GLOBAL attainment or an infinite counterfamily.

# Erdős Problem #99 — Wave94 full receipt harvest and Wave95 follow-up audit

Date: 2026-10-29, Europe/Brussels. ROOT agent maintains this record.

## Exact problem and result state

For each sufficiently large `n`, does **EVERY** ORIGINAL unrestricted GLOBAL
minimum-diameter unit-separated planar `n`-point set contain three ORIGINAL
points at all three pairwise distances **exactly 1**? This remains OPEN.
An arbitrary feasible triangle-free set, a selected global optimizer, a
finite `n=8` exception, and an asymptotically good lattice do not resolve the
eventual all-optimizer question. A negative result requires *infinitely many*
globally certified original triangle-free optima.

Official problem: https://www.erdosproblems.com/99 . Historical source:
https://mathematica-pannonica.ttk.pte.hu/articles/mp05-2/mp05-2-261-269.pdf .

## Native Maxwell: exact but currently unusable unique-diameter theorem

Native Sol Web High **Maxwell**, agent
`01a188d1-a1cb-7730-a82d-71c1f963ab35`, returned COMPLETED and was
CLOSED. Maxwell independently checked Wegener's earlier KKT proof:
if an unrestricted **local** unit-separated `n`-point diameter minimizer
has exactly one original diametral pair `pq`, then positive multipliers on
ORIGINAL unit contacts are all aligned with `pq`, the positive-contact
component must connect `p` to `q`, and that component is a straight
consecutive unit chain. Therefore its diameter `D` is a positive integer.
The MFCQ direction is global dilation of original coordinates; KKT's dyadic
rank-one identity has nonnegative contact weights. No auxiliary points.

**Important limitation:** Native Sol Web High **Sartre**, agent
`01a188dc-dbad-7823-b550-361058a06ba7`, returned COMPLETED and was
CLOSED. It independently validated a stronger theorem already in prior
canonical notes §2: for `n>=3`, NO original unrestricted *local* diameter
minimizer can have all diametral segments parallel, hence NONE can have a
unique diametral pair. Maxwell's implication is correct but vacuous for
these `n`; it must not be presented as substantive proof of eventual unit
triangles.

Independent proof of the nonparallel theorem: Suppose all diametral pairs
are horizontal and `D>1`. Vertically stretch all ORIGINAL points slightly;
diametral distances stay `D`, every initially non-diametral distance stays
strictly smaller than `D` for a sufficiently small stretch, and all
nonhorizontal unit contacts acquire strict slack. Remaining original
contacts are horizontal edges of length 1, disjoint paths, two-colorable
with alternating signs `s_i` in `{+1,-1}` on each edge. Then transform
original coordinates `(x_i,y_i)` (after the stretch) to
`(sqrt(1-t²)x_i, y_i+t*s_i/2)`. Each surviving original contact has length
exactly `sqrt((1-t²)+t²)=1`; all slack unit pairs remain at least 1 for
sufficiently small `t>0`. Each original diameter pair has new squared
length at most `(1-t²)D²+t² < D²`, while inactive diameter constraints
remain strict by finite slacks. Hence a strictly smaller-diameter
same-`n` feasible ORIGINAL point set exists, contradiction. When `D=1`
and `n>=3`, only an equilateral unit triangle fits, with nonparallel
diametral pairs. The surviving contact paths need not be connected. No
GLOBAL optimizer is assumed apart from local minimality.

Sartre's `n=8` exact global countermodel is the regular unit-side
heptagon plus its center, with `D8=1/(2 sin(π/14))`, no original unit
equilateral triple, and the center at distance
`R=1/(2 sin(π/7))>1` from all seven original vertices. Perturbing the
center by norm `<R-1` gives a continuum of original exact GLOBAL
optimizers without requiring all points to have unit contacts. This
refutes universal contact-degree, isolation, and selected-representative
extensions. Primary Bezdek–Fodor (1999):
https://doi.org/10.1006/jcta.1998.2889 .

The independent six-vertex regular hexagon perturbation at small `t>0`:
`p_k(t)=(1+(-1)^k*t)*(cos(kπ/3), sin(kπ/3))/sqrt(1+3t²)`;
all six adjacent original unit distances remain exactly 1, while every
opposite diagonal becomes `2/sqrt(1+3t²)<2`. Thus positive first-order
equilibrium stresses do **not** suffice for local diameter minimality.
Earlier exact ROOT verification: `work/erdos99/audit-wave92-root.py`.

Sartre also restated the older Oler-based `D9>=2.303895...` bound, which
is **weaker** than already verified strict Wegner-based `D9>2.315183...`.
No stronger `D9` result is credited from that repetition.

## Remaining decisive obstruction

A triangle-free original unit-contact graph has `e<=2n-4` by planarity,
including disconnected cases. Any all-global proof of `e>=2n-3` for every
sufficiently large optimizer would prove Erdős #99. Existing KKT,
second-order conditions, Oler/Wegner inequalities, diameter-graph covers,
and near-rhombic lattice estimates do **not** currently yield that global
unit-contact lower bound or a universal same-`n` strict descent.
No exact globally certified infinite triangle-free family has emerged.

Only ROOT/native owns local writes and verification. No GitHub changes,
publication, PR, or outbound correspondence.

# Erdős #99 — Wave96 root research audit (2026-10-29)

## Exact target and status

Let `D_n` be the global minimum diameter of any unit-separated set of exactly `n` original planar points. The question is whether, for all sufficiently large `n`, **every** exact unrestricted global optimizer has three **original** pairwise-unit-distance points. An infinite counterfamily would require exact, globally certified triangle-free optimizers. **OPEN; neither outcome has been proved.** Primary problem: https://www.erdosproblems.com/99 ; original Erdős (1994), §3.2: https://mathematica-pannonica.ttk.pte.hu/articles/mp05-2/mp05-2-261-269.pdf .

## Root mathematical synthesis: sharpened convex-hull deficit

Define `A=area(conv(X))`, `P=perimeter(conv(X))` and `D=D_n` for any ORIGINAL exact unrestricted global optimizer `X`, `n>=3`. The translated **open** disk of radius `D/2` in the unit triangular lattice cannot contain `n` lattice sites at any translation, since these would form an admissible diameter **strictly below** `D`. Thus the average-count/Fourier comparison, independently supported by W95_913, W96_920 and native Mendel, gives

`n-1 >= pi D^2/(2sqrt(3)) + Phi(D)`,

where `Phi(D)=max[D|J_1(2pi D/sqrt(3))|/2, D|J_1(4pi D/sqrt(3))|/4] >= 0`. Oler's exact inequality for the convex hull gives `n-1 <= 2A/sqrt(3)+P/2`. Rearranging,

`A >= pi D^2/4 + sqrt(3)Phi(D)/2 - sqrt(3)P/4`.

By `P<=pi D` and the isodiametric inequality `A<=pi D^2/4`, the **all-original, all-global** area deficit obeys

`0 <= delta := pi D^2/4-A <= pi sqrt(3) D/4 - sqrt(3)Phi(D)/2 <= pi sqrt(3) D/4`.

This strictly improves worker 924's more conservative `+sqrt(3)/2` constant and preserves the nonnegative Bessel correction. Using the standard Bonnesen inequality `P^2-4pi A >= pi^2 (R_out-r_in)^2` for circumradius `R_out` and inradius `r_in`, obtain

`0 <= R_out-r_in <= 2 sqrt(delta/pi) <= 3^(1/4) sqrt(D)`.

Since a diameter pair forces `R_out>=D/2` and `r_in>=R_out-(R_out-r_in)`, the original convex hull contains a disk of radius `D/2-O(sqrt D)` and fits inside one of radius `D/2+O(sqrt D)` (possibly requiring adjustment of centers). These are **necessary global hull geometry inequalities only**; they provide no exact original unit-contact count. The source of Oler's theorem is [Oler 1961](https://doi.org/10.4153/CMB-1961-018-7); Bonnesen and the exact Fourier argument are independently mathematical steps subject to ordinary mathematical verification, with no claimed publication priority.

`Omega = B intersect (intersection over u in U of {z: 1<=|z-u|<=d})`.

The U-to-replacement **upper** distance constraint `|z-u|<=d` is essential. If some translate of the unit triangular lattice (`a=sqrt(3)/2` cell area) has `k` points `S` in `Omega`, the SAME-n replacement `U union S` is unit-separated, and all its distances are at most `max(delta,d)<D`: distances within `U` by `delta`, within `S` by `diam(B)=d`, and across `U,S` by the defining annular constraints. Moreover, because `Omega` is compact, **strict** inequality holds for `k>=2`: if equality held, `N(t)=k-1` almost everywhere; upper semicontinuity of integer-valued `N` forces equality everywhere, making each locally finite summand `1_Omega(t+lambda)` both upper and lower semicontinuous, hence continuous. **Claim:** At least one original contact `ij∈E` obeys `v_i=v_j` for every `v∈L`. """Enumerate convex straight-thrackle forests and test positive equilibrium."""
import argparse, json
from collections import Counter
import numpy as np
from scipy.optimize import linprog

def compatible(e, f):
    a, b = e; c, d = f
    if len({a, b, c, d}) < 4:
        return True  # shared endpoint
    return (a < c < b) != (a < d < b)  # strict crossing

def representative(edges, n):
    images = []
    for sign in (1, -1):
        for shift in range(n):
            transformed = tuple(sorted(tuple(sorted(((sign*a+shift)%n,
                (sign*b+shift)%n))) for a, b in edges))
            images.append(transformed)
    return min(images)

def lp_stress(n, chords, tol):
    """Chord struts push out; all polygon-side cables pull in."""
    k = len(chords)
    theta = 2 * np.pi * np.arange(n) / n
    p = np.column_stack((np.cos(theta), np.sin(theta)))
    A = np.zeros((2 * n + 1, k + n + 1))
    for col, (i, j) in enumerate(chords):
        d = p[i] - p[j]
        A[2*i:2*i+2, col] += d
        A[2*j:2*j+2, col] -= d
    for side in range(n):
        i, j = side, (side + 1) % n
        d = p[i] - p[j]
        A[2*i:2*i+2, k+side] -= d
        A[2*j:2*j+2, k+side] += d
    A[2*n, :k] = 1  # sum chord lambda = 1
    b = np.zeros(2*n+1)
    b[-1] = 1
    ub = np.zeros((k+n, k+n+1))
    ub[np.arange(k+n), np.arange(k+n)] = -1
    ub[:, -1] = 1  # each lambda and mu >= t
    obj = np.zeros(k+n+1)
    obj[-1] = -1  # maximize t
    sol = linprog(obj, A_ub=ub, b_ub=np.zeros(k+n),
                  A_eq=A, b_eq=b,
                  bounds=[(0, None)] * (k+n+1),
                  method="highs",
                  options={"primal_feasibility_tolerance": 1e-9,
                           "dual_feasibility_tolerance": 1e-9})
    if not sol.success:
        return None
    residual = float(np.max(np.abs(A @ sol.x - b)))
    margin = float(min(sol.x[-1], np.min(sol.x[:-1])))
    if residual > 1e-7 or margin <= tol:
        return None
    return {"margin": margin,
            "min_lambda": float(np.min(sol.x[:k])),
            "min_mu": float(np.min(sol.x[k:k+n])),
            "max_eq_residual": residual}

def evaluate(n, target, tol):
    edges = [(i, j) for i in range(n) for j in range(i+1, n)
             if j-i != 1 and j-i != n-1]
    m = len(edges); edge_cover = [(1 << i) | (1 << j) for i, j in edges]
    compat = [sum(1 << j for j in range(m)
                  if i != j and compatible(edges[i], edges[j]))
              for i in range(m)]
    full = (1 << n) - 1; maxstep = (n-1)//2
    star_by_label = {i: tuple(sorted((i, (i+maxstep)%n)))
                     for i in range(n)}
    star = set(star_by_label.values())
    counts = Counter(); proper = []; orbits = Counter()
    def root(parent, x):
        while x != parent[x]:
            x = parent[x]
        return x
    def attainable(avail):
        seen = 0
        while avail:
            bit = avail & -avail
            seen |= edge_cover[bit.bit_length()-1]
            avail ^= bit
        return seen
    def dfs(chosen, available, parent, covered):
        left = target - len(chosen)
        if left == 0:
            if covered != full:
                return
            counts["covering_forests"] += 1
            pattern = [edges[i] for i in chosen]
            stress = lp_stress(n, pattern, tol)
            if stress is None:
                return
            chosen_set = set(pattern)
            missing = sorted(i for i, e in star_by_label.items()
                             if e not in chosen_set)
            is_special = (target == n-2 and chosen_set <= star and
                          len(missing) == 2 and
                          (missing[1]-missing[0]) % n in (1, n-1))
            rep = representative(pattern, n)
            orbits[rep] += 1
            proper.append({"chords": [list(e) for e in pattern],
                "all_longest": chosen_set <= star,
                "n_minus_2_star_adjacent_missing": is_special,
                "missing_star_start_labels": missing if chosen_set <= star else None,
                **stress})
            return
        if available.bit_count() < left:
            return
        unseen = full & ~covered
        if unseen.bit_count() > 2*left:
            return
        if unseen & ~attainable(available):
            return
        rest = available
        while rest:
            bit = rest & -rest
            rest ^= bit
            idx = bit.bit_length()-1
            a, b = edges[idx]
            ra, rb = root(parent, a), root(parent, b)
            if ra == rb:
                continue  # forest: never close a cycle
            new_parent = list(parent)
            new_parent[ra] = rb
            dfs(chosen + (idx,), rest & compat[idx],
                tuple(new_parent), covered | edge_cover[idx])
    dfs((), (1 << m)-1, tuple(range(n)), 0)
    return {"n": n, "chord_count": target, "candidate_chords": m,
        "counts": dict(counts), "proper_count": len(proper),
        "all_proper_are_n_minus_2_star_adjacent_missing":
            (all(x["n_minus_2_star_adjacent_missing"] for x in proper)
             if proper else None),
        "proper_patterns": proper,
        "dihedral_orbits": [{"representative": [list(e) for e in rep],
            "count": count} for rep, count in sorted(orbits.items())]}

def main():
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    ap.add_argument("--n", nargs="+", type=int, default=[7, 9])
    ap.add_argument("--tol", type=float, default=1e-8)
    args = ap.parse_args()
    if any(n < 5 or n % 2 == 0 for n in args.n) or args.tol <= 0:
        ap.error("n must be odd and >= 5; tol must be positive")
    reports = [evaluate(n, k, args.tol)
               for n in args.n for k in (n-2, n-1)]
    print(json.dumps({
        "scope": "All non-side chords; shared endpoint or strict crossing; "
                 "acyclic and vertex-covering; positive struts and all "
                 "boundary cables in full 2D equilibrium. Numerical LP "
                 "filter, not an exact or global-optimality certificate.",
        "tol": args.tol, "results": reports
    }, indent=2))

if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

"""Exact rational interval verification of worker423's hendecagon IFT data.

No floating-point arithmetic, nonlinear solver, or optimization is used.
Intervals are integer multiples of 10^-15, rounded outward at every
multiplication/division. Initial trigonometric enclosures use Machin's
identity, alternating arctangent series, and rational Taylor remainders.
"""
from dataclasses import dataclass
from fractions import Fraction as F
from itertools import permutations
from math import factorial
from pathlib import Path
import json

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
OUT = ROOT / "outputs" / "erdos99-hendecagon-ift-interval-exact.json"
SCALE = 10**15


def floor_fraction(x):
    return x.numerator // x.denominator


def ceil_fraction(x):
    return -((-x.numerator) // x.denominator)


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Interval:
    lo: int
    hi: int

    def __post_init__(self):
        if self.lo > self.hi:
            raise ValueError("Reversed interval")

    @staticmethod
    def from_fractions(lo, hi=None):
        lo = F(lo)
        hi = lo if hi is None else F(hi)
        return Interval(floor_fraction(lo * SCALE), ceil_fraction(hi * SCALE))

    @staticmethod
    def coerce(x):
        return x if isinstance(x, Interval) else Interval.from_fractions(x)

    def __add__(self, other):
        other = self.coerce(other)
        return Interval(self.lo + other.lo, self.hi + other.hi)

    __radd__ = __add__

    def __neg__(self):
        return Interval(-self.hi, -self.lo)

    def __sub__(self, other):
        return self + -self.coerce(other)

    def __rsub__(self, other):
        return self.coerce(other) + -self

    def __mul__(self, other):
        other = self.coerce(other)
        products = [a * b for a in (self.lo, self.hi)
                    for b in (other.lo, other.hi)]
        return Interval(min(products) // SCALE,
                        -((-max(products)) // SCALE))

    __rmul__ = __mul__

    def __truediv__(self, other):
        other = self.coerce(other)
        if other.lo <= 0 <= other.hi:
            raise ZeroDivisionError("Divisor interval contains zero")
        values = [F(a, b) for a in (self.lo, self.hi)
                  for b in (other.lo, other.hi)]
        return Interval.from_fractions(min(values), max(values))

    def contains_zero(self):
        return self.lo <= 0 <= self.hi

    def strictly_between(self, lower, upper):
        return self.lo > lower * SCALE and self.hi < upper * SCALE

    def report(self):
        return {
            "lower_scaled_integer": self.lo,
            "upper_scaled_integer": self.hi,
            "scale": SCALE,
            "lower_rational": str(F(self.lo, SCALE)),
            "upper_rational": str(F(self.hi, SCALE)),
        }


ZERO = Interval.from_fractions(0)


def atan_interval(reciprocal, terms):
    x = F(1, reciprocal)
    partial = sum(((-1)**j) * x**(2*j+1) / (2*j+1)
                  for j in range(terms))
    next_term = x**(2*terms+1) / (2*terms+1)
    if terms % 2 == 0:
        return partial, partial + next_term
    return partial - next_term, partial


atan5 = atan_interval(5, 18)
atan239 = atan_interval(239, 6)
PI_LO = 16 * atan5[0] - 4 * atan239[1]
PI_HI = 16 * atan5[1] - 4 * atan239[0]
assert F(314159, 100000) < PI_LO < PI_HI < F(314160, 100000)


def trig_intervals(angle_numerator):
    coeff = F(angle_numerator, 22)
    endpoints = (coeff * PI_LO, coeff * PI_HI)
    angle_lo, angle_hi = min(endpoints), max(endpoints)
    midpoint = (angle_lo + angle_hi) / 2
    uncertainty = (angle_hi - angle_lo) / 2
    # All |a_j^0| are below 1.3; Taylor terms decrease in magnitude.
    assert abs(midpoint) < F(13, 10)
    sine = sum(((-1)**j) * midpoint**(2*j+1) / factorial(2*j+1)
               for j in range(15))  # through degree 29
    cosine = sum(((-1)**j) * midpoint**(2*j) / factorial(2*j)
                 for j in range(15))  # through degree 28
    sine_error = abs(midpoint)**31 / factorial(31) + uncertainty
    cosine_error = abs(midpoint)**30 / factorial(30) + uncertainty

def crossing(e,f):
    a,b=e
    c,d=f
    return len(set(e+f))==4 and (a<c<b<d or c<a<d<b)


def thrackle(graph):
    return all(bool(set(e)&set(f)) or crossing(e,f)
               for e,f in combinations(graph,2))


def acyclic(graph):
    parents=list(range(N))
    def root(v):
        while parents[v]!=v:
            v=parents[v]
        return v
    for a,b in graph:
        ra,rb=root(a),root(b)
        if ra==rb:
            return False
        parents[ra]=rb
    return True

    return min(tuple(sorted(tuple(sorted(((sign*a+shift)%N,

import json

import numpy as np
from scipy.optimize import brentq

def check(length):
    eps=1/length
    def angle(beta):
        return beta/2+np.arcsin(eps*np.sin(beta/2))
    def residual(beta):
        alpha=angle(beta)
        return 2*(1+np.cos(alpha))*(1+eps)+eps**2-4*np.sin(beta)**2
    beta=brentq(residual,2*np.pi/5,np.pi/2,xtol=1e-14)
    alpha=angle(beta)
    uplus=np.array([-np.cos(alpha),np.sin(alpha)])
    uminus=uplus*np.array([1,-1])
    vplus=np.array([np.cos(beta),np.sin(beta)])
    vminus=vplus*np.array([1,-1])
    points=[np.array([0.,0.]),np.array([1.,0.])]
    edges=[(0,1)]; ends=[]
    for hub,direction in ((0,uplus),(0,uminus),(1,vplus),(1,vminus),(1,np.array([1.,0.]))):
        previous=hub
        for j in range(1,length+1):
            index=len(points);points.append(points[hub]+j*direction)
            edges.append((previous,index));previous=index
        ends.append(previous)
    p=np.array(points)
    xp,xm,yp,ym,z=ends
    diam_edges=[(xp,z),(xm,z),(xp,ym),(xm,yp),(yp,ym)]
    weight_a=1.
    weight_b=(length+1)*np.sin(alpha)/(length*np.sin(beta-alpha)-np.sin(alpha))
    weight_c=weight_b*(length*np.sin(beta-alpha)+np.sin(beta))/(2*length*np.cos(beta)*np.sin(beta))
    weights=np.array([weight_a,weight_a,weight_b,weight_b,weight_c])
    weights/=sum(weights)
    forces=np.zeros_like(p)
    for (i,j),lam in zip(diam_edges,weights):
        f=lam*(p[i]-p[j]);forces[i]+=f;forces[j]-=f
    mus=[float(forces[xp]@uplus),float(forces[xm]@uminus),
         float(forces[yp]@vplus),float(forces[ym]@vminus),float(forces[z,0])]
    contact_weights=[2*mus[0]*np.cos(alpha)]
    contact_weights+=sum(([mu]*length for mu in mus),[])
    residual_force=forces.copy()
    for (i,j),mu in zip(edges,contact_weights):
        f=mu*(p[i]-p[j]);residual_force[i]-=f;residual_force[j]+=f
    ii,jj=np.triu_indices(len(p),1);dist2=np.sum((p[ii]-p[jj])**2,axis=1)
    contact_set={tuple(sorted(e)) for e in edges}
    dia_set={tuple(sorted(e)) for e in diam_edges}
    noncontact=np.array([tuple(e) not in contact_set for e in zip(ii,jj)])
    nondia=np.array([tuple(e) not in dia_set for e in zip(ii,jj)])
    diameter=2*length*np.sin(beta)
    actual_contact={tuple(e) for e,d in zip(zip(ii,jj),dist2) if abs(d-1)<1e-8}
    actual_dia={tuple(e) for e,d in zip(zip(ii,jj),dist2) if abs(d-diameter**2)<1e-7}
    assert actual_contact==contact_set
    assert actual_dia==dia_set
    assert min(dist2[noncontact])>1+1e-7
    assert max(dist2[nondia])<diameter**2-1e-5
    assert min(contact_weights)>0 and min(weights)>0
    assert np.max(np.abs(residual_force))<1e-8
    laplacian=np.zeros((len(p),len(p)))
    for edge,weight in list(zip(diam_edges,weights))+[(edge,-mu) for edge,mu in zip(edges,contact_weights)]:
        i,j=edge
        laplacian[i,i]+=weight;laplacian[j,j]+=weight
        laplacian[i,j]-=weight;laplacian[j,i]-=weight
    eigenvalues=np.linalg.eigvalsh(laplacian)
    return {'L':length,'n':len(p),'D':float(diameter),'alpha':float(alpha),'beta':float(beta),
            'root_equation_residual':float(residual(beta)),
            'intended_contact_edges':len(edges),'detected_contact_edges':len(actual_contact),
            'actual_diameter_edges':len(actual_dia),
            'min_noncontact_squared':float(min(dist2[noncontact])),
            'max_force_residual':float(np.max(np.abs(residual_force))),
            'virial_residual':float(sum(contact_weights)-diameter**2),
            'min_contact_weight':float(min(contact_weights)),
            'stress_quadratic_max_eigenvalue_diagnostic':float(max(eigenvalues)),
            'stress_quadratic_positive_eigenvalues_tol1e-8':int(sum(eigenvalues>1e-8)),

Research Erdős #99 with a bounded independent assignment. D_n is the least diameter of n planar points with all pair distances>=1. Target: does EVERY exact global optimizer for all sufficiently large n contain an exact unit equilateral triangle? No resolution established. Return <=1500 words unless a full essential proof requires more, clear hypotheses/proofs/limitations and author/title/year/direct primary URLs. No new agents, publishing, contacting people, or artifact required. Never substitute approximate/global-affine optimality for unrestricted exact optimality.
Shared checked facts: triangle-free configurations have infimum D_n for EACH fixed n; arbitrarily small anisotropic stretch of an optimizer preserving one unit edge proves this. Every planar local diameter minimum with n>=3 has nonparallel diametral pairs (proved independently by root/native auditor and browser worker). Triangle-free convex edge-to-edge unit-rhombus tilings reduce to complete two-direction grids; root/native auditor proved only the unit square can be a local diameter minimum, by shifting an interior column perpendicular to its unit links, opening adjacent contacts quadratically and then compressing the width. Off-lattice/nonconvex boundary cases remain unhandled.
Literature update: Schurmann, On Extremal Finite Packings (2002), Theorem9, https://link.springer.com/content/pdf/10.1007/s00454-002-0747-6.pdf , already excludes sufficiently large exact diameter minimizers contained in ANY admissible packing lattice, uniformly over varying lattices, without bar-rigidity. It does not exclude a large crystalline bulk with O(sqrt(n)) arbitrary off-lattice boundary points. Archit Das (2026), https://zenodo.org/records/22768362 , gives adapted stresses: contact weights mu>=0 and diametral lambda>=0 with sumlambda=1, summu=D_n^2 and equilibrium at every vertex; positive mu only on contacts whose endpoint velocities AGREE for every contact-bar flex satisfying v_i=v_j on all diametral pairs. This is a relative-velocity condition, not just zero first derivative. The proof uses straight-line flexes opening nonfrozen contacts quadratically, nearby same-diameter optimizers, and a compact limit of normalized KKT stresses. No positivity on all contacts or co-large support is known.
'@

# Audit: finite inversion-even frozen-contact elimination

**Verdict: §1 of the central-symmetry draft is valid.** Normalize the chosen velocities, or budget actual displacement norms, when implementing the summable step-size sentence. No maximal-support stress selection or lexicographic selection is used.

This audit covers only the elimination dynamics and the terminal local-minimum/KKT transfer, not the later terminal geometry.

## Initial diameter graph

Let \(P^0=(p_i)\) be the original centrally symmetric, labeled unit-separated configuration, with involution \(\iota\), and assume \(D>1\). If \(R=\max_i|p_i|\), then \(D=2R\). Equality
\[
|p_i-p_k|\le |p_i|+|p_k|\le2R
\]
forces \(|p_i|=|p_k|=R\) and \(p_k=-p_i\). Thus every original diameter edge belongs to the matching \(\{i,\iota(i)\}\). A possible fixed label at the symmetry center is incident to no diameter edge.

## One exact elimination step

At a current configuration \(P^j=(q_i)\), assume:

- its complete diameter graph is the original \(H\);
- its complete unit graph \(F_j\) is an \(\iota\)-invariant subset of the original unit graph;
- every oriented vector on \(F_j\cup H\) equals its original vector.

Let
\[
W_j=\{v:\ v_{\iota(i)}=v_i,\ 
(q_i-q_k)\cdot(v_i-v_k)=0\ \text{for every }ik\in F_j\}.
\]
This is exactly the draft's space because the active vectors are unchanged.

For each nonfrozen edge, \(\{v\in W_j:v_i=v_k\}\) is a proper linear subspace by definition. A finite union of such subspaces cannot exhaust \(W_j\). Therefore one velocity can be chosen with \(v_i\ne v_k\) on every nonfrozen edge; normalize it to have norm \(1\).

Under \(q_i(t)=q_i+tv_i\):

1. Every \(H\)-vector is fixed, since its endpoints are \(\iota\)-partners.
2. Every frozen unit vector is fixed.
3. Every nonfrozen unit edge satisfies exactly
   \[
   |q_i(t)-q_k(t)|^2
   =1+t^2|v_i-v_k|^2>1\qquad(t\ne0).
   \]

All old nonunit pairs have strict lower slack, and all pairs outside \(H\) have strict upper slack. There are finitely many pairs, so a sufficiently small nonzero \(t\) preserves every such strict inequality. In particular, opened unit edges remain below \(D\), and no new contact or diameter edge appears. Thus the next complete unit graph is exactly the frozen subgraph and the complete diameter graph remains exactly \(H\).

For every even velocity,
\[
v_{\iota(i)}-v_{\iota(k)}=v_i-v_k.
\]
Hence an edge is frozen if and only if its opposite edge is frozen. The surviving graph is \(\iota\)-invariant. Its vectors, and all \(H\)-vectors, are unchanged. This proves the full induction even after global geometric central symmetry is lost.

## Finite termination inside the original neighborhood

At every nonterminal step at least one contact is removed. There are at most \(|F_0|\) such steps. Removing constraints can unfreeze previously frozen edges, so the repeated recomputation in the draft is important; termination nevertheless follows from strict contact-count decrease.

Choose \(\delta>0\) with the configuration-space ball \(B(P^0,\delta)\subset U\). With unit-norm velocities, impose additionally
\[
|t_j|<\delta\,2^{-j-2}.
\]
These conditions are compatible with every finite-slack restriction, since \(t_j\) can be arbitrarily small and nonzero. All configurations remain within distance \(\delta/2\) of \(P^0\). Previously opened pairs may have tiny slack, but that slack is positive and can be protected at the next finite step.

The terminal configuration \(P_*\) is feasible, lies in \(U\), has diameter exactly \(D\), retains the original complete diameter graph, and has every remaining unit edge frozen for its terminal space \(W_*\).

Since \(U\) is open and all feasible configurations in \(U\) have diameter at least \(D\), \(P_*\) is itself an ordinary local diameter minimum.

## Explicit KKT transfer

Use a squared-diameter variable \(\tau\) and minimize \(\tau\), subject to all pair inequalities
\[
|q_i-q_k|^2-1\ge0,\qquad
\tau-|q_i-q_k|^2\ge0.
\]
At \((P_*,D^2)\), choose the direction
\[
\dot q_i=q_i,\qquad \dot\tau=2D^2+1.
\]
Every active unit inequality has derivative \(2>0\), and every active diameter inequality has derivative \(1>0\). This proves MFCQ directly, independently of any residual geometric symmetry.

KKT therefore gives nonnegative multipliers supported on \(F_*,H\). Stationarity in \(\tau\) gives
\[
\sum_H\lambda=1,
\]
and position stationarity gives the physical equilibrium equations
\[
\sum_{ik\in F_*}\mu_{ik}(q_i-q_k)
=\sum_{ik\in H}\lambda_{ik}(q_i-q_k).
\]
Taking their scalar product with the positions and summing gives the virial identity
\[
\sum_{F_*}\mu=D^2.
\]
Thus the certificate is normalized and nontrivial. If the terminal contact graph were empty, this identity would already contradict the assumed local minimum.

The dynamics require only ordinary unit-separation feasibility \((\min\text{ distance}\ge1)\). If an exact-minimum-distance normalization is used and all contacts disappear, rescaling the resulting configuration gives an immediate strict diameter descent instead.

No maximum-support assumption is needed for any assertion audited here. The terminal stress-symmetrization and geometric classification are separate steps.

Date: 28 October 2026. Input: Root's `outputs/erdos99-central-symmetry-elimination-draft.md`. Verdict: Section 2 is correct conditional on Section 1's active-graph/vector invariants and existence of a normalized physical stress at the terminal packing. Neither a maximal-support selection nor mixed rigidity is needed. This does not audit the finite elimination or the terminal counting/classification, which have separate reviewers.

## 1. Explicit assumptions used

Write p_i for the ORIGINAL centrally symmetric packing, with center zero, and iota for its label involution, p_{iota(i)}=-p_i. There can be one fixed label at the original origin.

Write x_i for the terminal positions P*. The assumptions from Section 1 are:

- P* is a genuine unit-separated packing of actual diameter D>1.
- Its FULL current unit graph F* is iota-invariant.
- Its FULL current diameter graph is the original H. Each edge of H is an antipodal-label pair {i,iota(i)}.
- For every edge ij of F* or H, the directed current difference equals the original one:

       x_i-x_j = p_i-p_j.

- There exists a nonnegative physical equilibrium stress (lambda,mu) on H,F*, normalized by sum_H lambda=1.

The last existence statement is supplied by the draft's KKT step and is not independently re-audited here. For this section the important property is NONNEGATIVE physical equilibrium, not maximal support.

## 2. Relabeling preserves the physical stress cone, with correct signs

For weights s=(lambda,mu), define the unit-minus-diameter force at label i by

    E_i(s) = sum_{ij in F*} mu_ij (x_i-x_j)
             - sum_{ik in H} lambda_ik (x_i-x_k).

Equilibrium is E_i(s)=0 at every label. Define pullback weights

    mu^iota_ij = mu_{iota(i),iota(j)},
    lambda^iota_ik = lambda_{iota(i),iota(k)}.

Both active graphs are invariant, so these are weights on the SAME current active rows. The directed-vector invariant and original central symmetry give

    x_{iota(i)}-x_{iota(j)}
      = p_{iota(i)}-p_{iota(j)}
      = -(p_i-p_j)
      = -(x_i-x_j)

for every currently active unit or diameter edge. Reindexing each neighbor sum therefore gives the exact identity

    E_i(s^iota) = -E_{iota(i)}(s).

Thus s^iota is another physical equilibrium stress. The global minus is harmless and is the same for contact and diameter forces. There is no orientation-dependent change in the signs of the nonnegative edge coefficients. On H every unordered edge is itself fixed by iota, so in fact lambda^iota=lambda individually.

The pullback is a linear involution on the nonnegative physical stress cone and preserves its normalized slice. Consequently

    s_bar = (s+s^iota)/2

is a nonnegative normalized physical stress satisfying s_bar^iota=s_bar. Its unit support is invariant under iota. Virial gives sum mu_bar=D^2>0, so its positive unit support is nonempty.

This argument would NOT follow from preservation of active lengths alone. It uses the stated directed-vector relation on every current active edge. No central symmetry of the entire terminal point set is assumed.

## 3. Exactly what the accepted connectivity lemma supplies

Verified notes Section 19 states that for ANY nonnegative normalized physical contact/diameter stress of a planar unit packing with D>1, the positive unit graph has exactly one nontrivial component, and it contains every endpoint of every positive diameter edge. It requires neither central symmetry, local optimality, triangle-freeness, nor maximal support.

Its proof uses exposed diameter endpoints, planar contact paths and a noncrossing loaded-endpoint partition, rather than a symmetry assumption.

Let T denote this unique nontrivial positive unit component, including its endpoint vertices. Since mu_bar is invariant, iota sends positive unit components to positive unit components. Uniqueness therefore gives iota(T)=T. It is not necessary to assert that an arbitrary unaveraged certificate already has invariant unit support.

Normalization supplies at least one positive diameter edge. The lemma puts BOTH of its endpoints in T. Thus T has geometric span D.

Zero-stress vertices and other full contact components have not been discarded. The lemma does not assert that every actual diameter endpoint is positively loaded. Actual zero-weight diameter pairs may still have endpoints outside T or outside the full component selected below.

## 4. The invariant FULL contact component

Let C be the full F* connected component containing T. This component is unambiguously defined because T is connected and nonempty.

The label involution is an automorphism of the FULL current unit graph F*. Therefore iota(C) is a full component. It contains iota(T)=T, so it is the same component C. Thus iota(C)=C.

This step allows all zero-weight unit edges and vertices in C. Other full components may be invariant separately or exchanged by iota; their behavior is irrelevant. The result concerns one invariant full component, not invariance of every full component.

    x_{iota(i)}=-p_i+t_C=2t_C-x_i.

Hence the restricted terminal point set {x_i:i in C} is centrally symmetric about t_C. If the fixed original center label belongs to C, its terminal position is exactly t_C. This componentwise symmetry does not imply a common symmetry center for the rest of P*.

Its full unit graph is triangle-free because F* is an iota-invariant SUBGRAPH of the original triangle-free F. The component translation also preserves every internal original pair distance, not merely its surviving edge lengths.

# Audit of central-symmetry draft, Sections 3-4 only

## Verdict and assumed interfaces

Sections 3-4 pass under the stated conclusions of Sections 1-2. No counterexample was found. This audit does not verify the elimination dynamics, preservation of active vectors, or stress averaging in the earlier sections.

The precise interfaces used are:

1. C is a nontrivial connected FULL unit-contact component, invariant under the label involution iota; iota acts on it as central inversion about its translated center. It has diameter D.
2. Every inversion-even unit-bar velocity on C extends by zero to an allowed global terminal velocity. Every remaining unit edge is terminally frozen under all such velocities.
3. There is a nonnegative physical stress with a nonempty positive contact support T contained in C, and ALL endpoints of positive diameter edges belong to T and hence to C.
4. The full contact graph is triangle-free and the entire point set is unit-separated.

The third interface is important in the nonsquare case. It is supplied by Section 2, rather than by central symmetry of C alone.

## 1. The restricted dimension count

Let r and m be the vertex and edge counts of C. Let c be the number of fixed labels of iota in C; c is either zero or one. Let a be the number of unordered unit edges fixed by iota.

There are (r-c)/2 two-label orbits and c one-label orbits. An inversion-even velocity assigns one planar vector to each orbit, so its ambient dimension is

2[(r-c)/2+c]=r+c.

A fixed edge joins two antipodal labels. Its endpoint velocities are equal on this space, so its bar row vanishes identically. Every nonfixed edge belongs to a two-edge orbit. On even velocities, the two bar rows are negatives of each other: their geometric edge vectors are opposite while their velocity differences agree, using corresponding orientations. The restricted rank is therefore at most (m-a)/2. Hence

dim W_even(C) >= r+c-(m-a)/2.

Zero extension is valid because C is an invariant FULL contact component: there is no unit row crossing from C to another component, and all outside labels have velocity zero. Terminal freezing then forces every velocity in W_even(C) to be constant along every edge. Connectivity makes it a translation on C. Conversely every translation on C is such an extendible velocity. Thus the dimension is exactly two, and

m >= 2r+2c+a-4.                              (1)

The count uses ALL m unit edges of C, even if some have zero stress.

## 2. Euler and the outer walk

Unit separation makes the straight unit-contact graph plane and simple. Let b count the unit edge traversals in its outer facial walk, including bridges twice. With f=m-r+1 bounded faces, each bounded facial walk has length at least four, so

2m >= b+4f,
m <= 2r-2-b/2.                              (2)

Cutvertices, internal bridges, and repeated facial-walk edges do not alter these identities. Combining (1) and (2) gives exactly

b <= 4-4c-2a.                               (3)

The walk visits both endpoints of a diameter of C, since these are hull vertices. Its two portions between those visits each have Euclidean length at least D. Therefore b>=2D. This alone supplies the proposed contradiction for D>2.

## 3. Complete classification when b<=4

The component is nontrivial, so b>0. Equation (3) first forces c=0. Thus r is even.

If a>=1, then b<=2. A connected simple plane graph with outer walk length two is a single edge: that walk encloses no region in which further graph could be hidden. Its diameter is one. Hence this case cannot occur when D>sqrt(2).

Now take a=c=0. If C is a tree, b=2(r-1)<=4 gives r<=3. Evenness and nontriviality force r=2, but its only edge is then antipodally fixed, contradicting a=0.

If C has a cycle, its outer boundary must contain a cycle. Triangle-freeness makes that cycle at least four edges long. Since b<=4, the entire outer facial walk is a simple four-cycle. Equivalently, the only non-simple closed walks of length at most four in a simple triangle-free graph are tree backtracks; these cannot be the outer boundary of a graph containing a cycle. Thus bridges, holes, and cutvertices do not produce an additional case at this boundary budget.

The four unit sides form a nondegenerate convex rhombus. For example, the two other vertices are the two distinct intersections of the unit circles about either opposite pair, so they lie on opposite sides of that diagonal.

## 4. The rhombus contains no additional packing vertex

Let alpha in (0,pi/2] be its acute angle. Split along its shorter diagonal. Each resulting triangle has sides 1,1,2 sin(alpha/2), and circumradius

rho=1/[2 cos(alpha/2)] <= 1/sqrt(2) < 1.

For a point x of either triangle, take its nonnegative barycentric weights lambda_j and circumcenter O. The exact identity

sum_j lambda_j |x-v_j|^2 = rho^2-|x-O|^2 <= rho^2

shows that x lies within rho of at least one triangle vertex. Hence no additional unit-separated packing point can lie anywhere in the closed rhombus.

Since the simple four-cycle is the outer boundary of C, all its remaining vertices would have to lie in that closed rhombus. There are none. A unit diagonal between the four existing vertices would form a unit triangle, forbidden by triangle-freeness. Thus C is precisely the four-cycle. In particular, hidden blocks, cutvertices, bridges, or holes inside it are impossible.

## 5. Physical stress rules out a nonsquare rhombus

The rhombus has diameter D by the assumed span property. If nonsquare, only its longer diagonal has length D. Its two other, opposite vertices are not endpoints of any internal diameter pair.

The assumed conclusion of draft Section 2 confines every POSITIVE diameter edge to C. Consequently the two short-diagonal vertices have zero diameter load in the chosen stress. This remains true even if one contemplates zero-weight actual diameter constraints elsewhere in the entire configuration.

At either such vertex the full contact degree is two, with nonparallel incident unit vectors. Equilibrium with zero diameter load forces both contact weights to vanish. The two opposite vertices together cover all four sides, so every contact weight in C vanishes. This contradicts the nonempty positive contact support T contained in C.

Therefore the rhombus is square, and its diameter is sqrt(2).

## Final checked implication

Under the interfaces of Sections 1-2, a terminal stressed component of span D>sqrt(2) cannot exist. Thus the counting and finite geometry in Sections 3-4 provide the proposed contradiction if the earlier dynamical and symmetry steps are independently established.

No conclusion about those earlier steps, the full central-symmetry theorem, or the general Erdos problem is promoted by this audit alone.

# Folkman–Graham 1969: perimeter, topology, and residual-region scope

Audited 27 October 2026. Narrow primary-source check; the proposed residual-region geometry is not audited here.

## Primary source and pages

J. H. Folkman and R. L. Graham, *A Packing Inequality for Compact Convex Subsets of the Plane*, Canadian Mathematical Bulletin 12(6) (1969), 745–752. DOI: https://doi.org/10.4153/CMB-1969-096-7.

Primary PDF: https://www.cambridge.org/core/services/aop-cambridge-core/content/view/745BF5B96E3285103D53BCCE5D5B08AD/S000843950005428Xa.pdf/a-packing-inequality-for-compact-convex-subsets-of-the-plane.pdf

Saved locally as `audit-circular-folkman-graham1969.pdf`. Printed p.746 was visually inspected in `audit-circular-folkman-graham1969-p2.png`.

## Paraphrase of the primary definitions and theorem

Printed pp.745–746 define finite geometric simplicial complexes in the plane, with intersections required to be shared faces. Global general position of the vertex set is not required: individual triangles must be nondegenerate.

On p.746, write e(sigma,K) for the number of triangles incident to an edge sigma. The definitions are

    A(K) = sum over triangles of their areas,
    P(K) = sum over edges sigma of (2 - e(sigma,K)) length(sigma),
    chi(K) = alpha_0(K) - alpha_1(K) + alpha_2(K).

The authors state that these depend only on the underlying polyhedron. Section 3, p.746, gives

    alpha_0(K) <= (2/sqrt(3)) A(K) + P(K)/2 + chi(K)

whenever every distinct pair of vertices is at Euclidean distance at least 1. The theorem imposes no connectedness, convexity, or hole-free restriction. Its proof concludes on p.751.

## Consequences of those definitions

For a triangulated polygonal region, an interior edge has two incident triangles and contributes zero to P. Every edge along any outer or hole boundary has one incident triangle and contributes its length once. An edge with no incident triangle contributes twice its length. An isolated vertex contributes no perimeter, but contributes one to alpha_0 and chi.

Thus all boundary components of a genuine two-dimensional polygonal region are counted, including hole boundaries. Shared seams between two filled sides are not counted. A discarded empty face does not contribute triangles, and its boundary edges are counted once if the other side is filled; an edge retained with neither side filled would count twice.

The Euler characteristic is the usual one. For a compact planar polyhedron, chi = b_0 - b_1 <= b_0, where b_0 is the number of connected components. This remains true for pinched regions. For disjoint ordinary polygonal domains, chi is the number of components minus the total number of holes.

## Triangulation deduction (not a separate quotation from the paper)

A finite polygonal region with holes can be triangulated using its boundary vertices, with no new geometric vertices: connect holes to outer boundaries by noncrossing visibility diagonals, then triangulate the resulting polygonal pieces. Collinear boundary vertices are retained by splitting boundary edges. Insert any further designated separated points by subdividing their containing triangles, or both adjacent triangles when a point lies on an edge. This introduces only the designated points. The resulting triangles and all their faces form a complex covered by the theorem.

The initial boundary must already be a planar straight-line complex: any necessary segment intersection or endpoint subdivision must be among the permitted separated vertices. The theorem does not license adding an unseparated Steiner vertex and then ignoring it in alpha_0. All points being counted must lie in the retained region.

## Conditional residual estimate

Suppose the proposed retained region R is such a polygonal polyhedron, all its boundary vertices and all t counted points belong to one unit-separated set, no isolated point or purely one-dimensional component is retained, and its full boundary length is J. With a_0 = sqrt(3)/2,

    t <= A(R)/a_0 + J/2 + chi(R).

Each positive-area component has at least one boundary edge, and every such edge has length at least 1 because its distinct endpoints belong to the separated set. Consequently chi(R) <= number of components <= number of boundary edges <= J, yielding

    t <= A(R)/a_0 + 3J/2.

This verifies the theorem's tool scope and the conditional algebra. It does not establish that the proposed rhombus-removal construction has the stipulated region, boundary vertices, retained points, or boundary-length bound.

# Graham–Witsenhausen–Zassenhaus 1972: exact zero-slack equality

Audited 27 October 2026. Primary-source equality classification only; no quantitative stability or global Erdős #99 theorem is established here.

## Source and inspected pages

R. L. Graham, H. S. Witsenhausen and H. J. Zassenhaus, *On tightest packings in the Minkowski plane*, Pacific Journal of Mathematics 41(3) (1972), 699–715.

DOI: https://doi.org/10.2140/pjm.1972.41.699. Publisher metadata confirms the page range and publication date 1 June 1972.

Primary PDF: https://msp.org/pjm/1972/41-3/pjm-v41-n3-p10-p.pdf.

The downloaded PDF is `audit-circular-graham-witsenhausen-zassenhaus1972.pdf`. Printed pp.714–715 were visually inspected and retained as images with those page numbers in their filenames.

## Primary statement, paraphrased

The paper defines Delta* on p.701 as the smallest area of a unit equilateral triangle in the chosen Minkowski norm; it is sqrt(3)/4 in Euclidean geometry. A finite packing, p.710, is a finite plane simplicial complex whose distinct visible vertices are at distance at least one: the segment joining the pair must lie in the support. Full pairwise separation is stronger.

Section 9, p.714, defines

    tau(K) = A(K)/(2 Delta*) + P(K)/2 + chi(K) - alpha_0(K).

Theorem 5, p.715: tau(K)=0 precisely when the same support admits a triangulation using the same vertex set, with every edge of length one and every triangular face a unit equilateral triangle of area Delta*. The existing triangulation need not already have this property; retriangulation is permitted. No additional vertices are authorized by this statement.

## Euclidean filled-Jordan-polygon specialization

Let J be the closed region bounded by a positive-area simple Jordan polygon. Suppose its b boundary edges all have length one, q additional designated points lie strictly inside J, and all b+q designated points are pairwise at distance at least one. Triangulate J using exactly these points. Then

    P(K)=b, chi(K)=1, alpha_0(K)=b+q, a_0=2 Delta*=sqrt(3)/2,

so the published slack is exactly

    tau(K)=sigma=A(J)/a_0 - b/2 + 1 - q.

Theorem 5 therefore gives the precise equivalence: sigma=0 iff J can be triangulated using ALL designated points and no others into unit equilateral triangles. In particular, positive area forces at least one triangular face, and hence the point set contains a unit equilateral triangle. No convexity hypothesis on J is needed.

For a direct converse check, a unit-equilateral triangulation has T=2q+b-2 triangular faces by Euler's formula and 3T=2E-b. Hence A(J)=T sqrt(3)/4, which gives sigma=0.

## General-complex limitation

The theorem does not require every edge to bound a triangular face. An isolated vertex has zero slack; a single unit segment has zero slack. Any admissible plane complex consisting only of unit edges and isolated vertices also has zero slack, because P=2E, chi=V-E and A=0. These are genuine examples, not counterexamples to Theorem 5.

A positive-area tight complex must contain some unit equilateral triangular face in its equality triangulation, but it can also have bare unit edges or isolated vertices. A Jordan CURVE considered only as a one-dimensional support must not be confused with its filled enclosed region.

## Attribution scope

Attribute the exact equality classification used here to Graham–Witsenhausen–Zassenhaus, Theorem 5 (1972). Their abstract and introduction, p.699, describe this as extending Oler's 1961 treatment of admissible Jordan triangulations; their bibliography identifies Oler's *An inequality in the geometry of numbers*, Acta Math.105 (1961), 19–48. The Folkman–Graham 1969 inequality is also an explicit predecessor.

The bare equality conclusion is therefore classical. Any new quantitative boundary-stability assertion needs a separate proof and does not inherit novelty from this equality import. No original Oler equality-theorem number has been verified in this audit.
